chunks: And similarly, the report narrated by Sa'd ibn Abdillah from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab from Dinār ibn Hakīm from al-Hārith from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

There is no harm in delaying the breaking of the fast (Iftar) until the crescent of Dhu al-Qa'dah. The aspect in this report is also what we said in the first report, equally, and that which indicates what we said.
ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to delay breaking the fast until the crescent of Dhu al-Qa'dah?
ai.summary: This report from *Al-Istibsar* clarifies the permissibility of delaying the *Fitrah* (often interpreted as the specific offering or the start of the fasting period in this context) until the sighting of the Dhu al-Qa'dah crescent, linking it to the legal reasoning of a preceding hadith. It reflects the Shia scholarly tradition of relying on continuous chains (*isnad*) from the Imams to establish flexible yet precise temporal rulings for religious obligations.
